_what_this_is: The author's record of having opened every page of the rendered
manuscript. The digests are of the page images, because a rebuild that
changes nothing produces a different .docx and a different PDF every
time while the page images come back byte-identical: a ledger pinning
the documents would be permanently red and would say nothing about what
looked_at_by: Claude Opus 5, on the author's instruction
note: Captions set italic after the run-in label, in addition to the 10 pt size, because two points alone did not read as a boundary -- the author said so after looking at page 7, where Figure 2's caption sat under the body in the same rhythm. The page ledger made this review cheap and exact: only 9 of 27 pages differed from the last review, the nine carrying a caption, and those nine were opened. p4 Figure 1 (italic 60-73, body resumes roman at 74), p7 Figure 2 (129-133, body 134), p8 Figure 3 opening (154-155), p9 Figure 3 continuation (156-160, heading 161), p12 Figure 4 (220-225, heading 226), p13 Table 1 (240-248, body 249 overleaf), p14 Figure 5 (254-259), p15 Figure 6 (265-274, body 275), p19 Figure 7 (337-339, heading 340). No caption carried an italic run of its own, which the builder checks rather than assumes, so nothing was hidden by the change. The other 18 pages are byte-identical to the ones reviewed earlier this evening; 27 pages still, line numbers 1-553 continuous.
